holidays.name: National Button Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble button, the small round fastener that holds shirts, coats and collections together. Dig out your button jar, sew on that missing one, or admire a vintage set.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its exact origin is unclear. It is a favorite among sewing and crafting fans.
holidays.funFact: Buttons were used as decoration long before they became fasteners. Buttonholes only appeared in Europe in the 13th century.

holidays.name: Have a Party With Your Bear Day
holidays.description: A day for a tea party, picnic or movie night with your favorite teddy bear. Stuffed animals get an invitation, and so does your inner child.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a whimsical nod to the cuddly companions many people grew up with.
holidays.funFact: The teddy bear is named after U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt. A 1902 hunting trip inspired a famous cartoon and then the toy.

holidays.name: International Check Your Wipers Day
holidays.description: A practical reminder to check your windshield wipers as the weather turns rainy, snowy and icy. Replace worn blades before the first big storm.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is marked in North America as winter driving season approaches.
holidays.funFact: The windshield wiper was patented by Mary Anderson in 1903, years before wipers were standard on cars.
